description: Inline the PAD-relative accesses to skip rd8/wr8's bounds check on the tokeniser path: 741 -> 637 B. The shared call wins because the call site pays the same address materialisation and the callee's arithmetic/test is shared across ~100 sites. Third local edit in a row to regress.

asi.lesson_inline: a shared callee beats inline code even when the inline code skips a check: the call site costs lui+addi+jal either way, and the callee's address arithmetic and bound test are shared across ~100 call sites. Inlining 9 sites cost +104 B. This is the third local edit in a row to regress (literal width, gp/small-data, PAD inlining), which is the signal that this file is at a local optimum and only structural change helps

description: Hoist w/ip out of the VM struct into dispatch-loop locals, flushing only at the three real leaves (EXIT switch, loop-tail switch, stack-overflow return). +16 B app space, text -16, and two fewer memory round-trips per token. Device-verified including recursion, a backward loop and two task switches.

asi.device: flashed at MEMSZ 1718: 2 3 + . = 5, 10 FIB . = 55, CNT (100-iteration BEGIN..UNTIL) = 100, two tasks printed 30 and 70 (the task-switch flush path), 15 FIB . = ERR_STACK, 0 BLOCK . = 1590 (= new BLKADR), 100 7 /MOD = 14 2, 2 3 + . = 5 after
asi.hypothesis: w and ip are u16 FIELDS of the VM struct, so every token read and wrote them in memory (twice per dispatch plus once per body touching ip: LIT, BRANCH, ZBRANCH, DOCOL, EXIT, EXEC). Hoist them into locals for the dispatch loop, flush only at the three real leaves (task switch from EXIT, task switch from the loop tail, stack-overflow return)
asi.measured: app 741 -> 757 (+16), text 4912 -> 4896. Also removes 2 memory round-trips per token, so it is a speed win as well
asi.next_action_hint: same shape applies to other VM scalars that are read per token: sp and rsp are u8 FEEDLS read on every PUSH/POP/DUP. They were NOT hoisted because bodies change them constantly and the flush surface would be every return; but a smarter split (keep sp in a local, write back only at calls that can observe it) may pay. Measure before believing
asi.risk_lesson: the flush surface is the whole risk: every exit path must VM_FLUSH or the next vm_enter resumes at the previous token and silently re-executes it. Found and fixed a real sloppiness on the way: redefining the w/ip macros produced two compiler warnings on every build, now #undef'd first and the file-scope originals restored after the function
